title: How many cowrie shells did the beggar get?
description: A miser gives a beggar a part of a dramma, found by taking a fraction of a fraction six times over. The six fractions are multiplied together, the product is brought to lowest form, and that part of one thousand two hundred eighty cowrie shells is taken. Keeko thinks only the numerators need to be multiplied.
teaching_notes: One idea: many fractions joined by of are multiplied as one product, numerators together and denominators together, and the result is reduced before it is used. Watch for students who multiply only the numerators and read that number as the answer.

source: A miser gave a beggar 1/5 of 1/16 of 1/4 of 1/2 of 2/3 of 3/4 of a dramma. If 1 dramma equals 1280 cowrie shells, how many cowrie shells did the beggar get?
video_script.why: A learner sees that a chain of fractions joined by of is one long product, which is reduced to lowest form before it is applied to the number of shells.
video_script.substitution: the book's own miser and beggar, with the six fractions of a dramma and the value of one thousand two hundred eighty cowrie shells
video_script.anchor: a dramma shown as a pile of one thousand two hundred eighty cowrie shells, with a chain of six fractions beside it
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies only the numerators of the six fractions and reads the product six as the number of shells
video_script.payoff_line: The beggar got one cowrie shell.
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, two thirds, three quarters, one fifth, one sixteenth, one quarter, six over seven thousand six hundred eighty, one over one thousand two hundred eighty
maths_rules: the part of a dramma = 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 x 1/5 x 1/16 x 1/4
numerators: 1 x 2 x 3 x 1 x 1 x 1 = 6
denominators: 2 x 3 x 4 x 5 x 16 x 4 = 7680
the slip: reading the numerator product 6 as the number of shells
video_script.design: A dramma drawn as a pile of cowrie shells; the chain of six fractions is written under it and multiplied in one line, then reduced, then applied to the pile.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a miser with a pile of shells, a beggar holding out a hand, and a chain of six fractions

marks.miser: the miser and the beggar appear beside the pile of shells
marks.parts: the chain of six fractions is written one by one
marks.ask: the value of one dramma appears and the beggar's hand flashes

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book, from an old text about money.
<bookmark mark='miser'/>A miser gave a beggar a tiny part of a dramma.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>Start with three quarters of a dramma, and take two thirds of that.
Then take half of that, then one quarter, then one sixteenth, and then one fifth.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>One dramma equals one thousand two hundred eighty cowrie shells.
How many cowrie shells did the beggar get?

beats.on_screen: the pile of shells and the chain of fractions stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the pile of shells; each fraction in the chain takes a smaller piece of what is left

marks.pile: the pile of one thousand two hundred eighty shells is drawn as one dramma
marks.of: the word of is written with a times sign above it
marks.rule: a numerator row and a denominator row are drawn under the chain

narration: <bookmark mark='pile'/>Each fraction in the chain takes a smaller piece of what is left of the dramma.
<bookmark mark='of'/>Each time the word of means times, so the fractions are multiplied.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The numerators multiply together, and the denominators multiply together.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1/5 of 1/16 of 1/4 of 1/2 of 2/3 of 3/4 of a dramma; 1 dramma = 1280 cowrie shells

marks.given: the chain of fractions is written
marks.value: the value of one dramma is written below it

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the beggar gets a part of a dramma, made of six fractions.
<bookmark mark='value'/>One dramma equals one thousand two hundred eighty cowrie shells.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of cowrie shells the beggar gets

marks.find: the words number of cowrie shells are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of cowrie shells the beggar gets.

marks.chain: the six fractions are written as one product

narration: <bookmark mark='chain'/>Step one, of means times, so multiply all six fractions.
One half times two thirds times three quarters times one fifth times one sixteenth times one quarter.

beats.on_screen: numerators: 1 × 2 × 3 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 6;  denominators: 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 × 16 × 4 = 7680;  so the part is 6/7680

marks.frac: the fraction six over seven thousand six hundred eighty is written

narration: <bookmark mark='num'/>Step two, multiply the numerators.
One times two times three is six, and the other numerators are one.
<bookmark mark='den'/>Multiply the denominators, two times three times four times five times sixteen times four.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>The product is seven thousand six hundred eighty.

beats.on_screen: 6/7680 = 1/1280  (divide the top and the bottom by 6)

marks.low: six over seven thousand six hundred eighty is written
marks.div: the top and the bottom are divided by six
marks.frac: one over one thousand two hundred eighty is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step three, write the fraction in lowest form.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide the top and the bottom by six.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>That gives one over one thousand two hundred eighty.

marks.of: one over one thousand two hundred eighty of one thousand two hundred eighty is written
marks.mult: the product is written as one thousand two hundred eighty over one thousand two hundred eighty

narration: <bookmark mark='of'/>Step four, the beggar gets that fraction of one thousand two hundred eighty cowrie shells.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Multiply one over one thousand two hundred eighty by one thousand two hundred eighty.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed beside one shell
marks.same: the same number over itself is written as one

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The beggar got one cowrie shell.
<bookmark mark='same'/>One thousand two hundred eighty over the same number is one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the chain of fractions
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 1 × 2 × 3 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 6 shells crossed out; the denominators 7680 shown under the numerator 6

marks.doubt: the product of the numerators is written as six shells
marks.den: the denominator seven thousand six hundred eighty appears under the six
marks.fix: six shells is crossed out and the fraction returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks six cowrie shells are given, after multiplying only the numerators.
<bookmark mark='den'/>But six is only the top of the fraction.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The denominators must be multiplied too, and then the fraction is brought to lowest form.
